c01s03.title: Different questions
right: How did it arise or persist?
c01s03.caption: A historical account is not a reading of a current intention.

c01s03b.title: Four questions, distinct evidence
items: How does it emerge in a lifetime?
How did it evolve, and with what consequences?
c01s03b.caption: The final row includes two distinct evolutionary questions.

c01s04.title: Turn a story into a hypothesis
c01s04.caption: A plausible function is a research question rather than a settled fact.

c01s05.title: Choose the question before the answer
c01s05.caption: Different explanations need different evidence.

c02s03.title: A selection explanation
c02s03.caption: The process requires conditions, not an intention to improve the species.

c02s03b.title: Different meanings of better
c02s03b.caption: Evolutionary terminology does not define what society should value.

c02s04.title: Alternative processes
c02s04.caption: Existence alone does not demonstrate adaptive function.

c02s05.title: Check a selection story
c02s05.caption: Selection is a mechanism to investigate, not a synonym for usefulness.

c03s03.title: Present use and origin
left: What does the feature do now?
c03s03.caption: Current usefulness does not uniquely identify historical selection.

c03s03b.title: Evaluate an adaptation claim
c03s03b.caption: The strength lies in discriminating evidence rather than narrative appeal.

c03s04.title: A mismatch question
c03s04.caption: A contrast must be evidenced rather than imagined as a uniform ancestral life.

c03s05.title: A stronger origin argument
c03s05.caption: A good evolutionary account is vulnerable to relevant evidence.

c04s03.title: A capacity develops
c04s03.caption: The influences interact rather than contribute as separate personal percentages.

c04s03b.title: Different questions
left: Why do people in this sample differ?
c04s03b.caption: A variance estimate is not a complete developmental mechanism.

c04s04.title: A learning-origin claim
c04s04.caption: Evidence for a learning bias needs more than a present preference.

c04s05.title: Keep the levels distinct
c04s05.caption: Related questions still require different evidence.

c05s03.title: A kin-selection question
c05s03.caption: The framework concerns evolutionary consequences rather than conscious arithmetic.

c05s03b.title: Model quantities need definition
c05s03b.caption: A symbolic rule is not an explanation until its quantities fit the case.

c05s04.title: Avoid the only-cause claim
c05s04.caption: A partial explanation does not exclude other forms of helping.

c05s05.title: A bounded kin-selection explanation
c05s05.caption: A formal evolutionary account has a specific scope.

c06s03.title: Different cooperative settings
c06s03.caption: Modelled conditions shape predictions; actual life may not match them.

c06s03b.title: A possible reputation pathway
c06s03b.caption: Reputation is one possible influence rather than a unique motive.

c06s04.title: Three possible contributions
c06s04.caption: Cooperation can arise through several interacting processes.

c06s05.title: A cooperation claim needs conditions
c06s05.caption: Cooperation is a research problem rather than a single hidden motive.

c07s03.title: Keep the model specific
items: What does the model leave out?
c07s03.caption: A reproductive model is not a complete account of human intimacy.

c07s03b.title: Model and overgeneralization
c07s03b.caption: A model must retain its conditions and individual variability.

c07s04.title: Average and individual
right: Cannot be read from the average
c07s04.caption: Population differences do not identify an individual’s choices.

c07s05.title: A responsible relationship claim
c07s05.caption: Human relationships cannot be reduced to a universal ancestral script.

c08s03.title: A transmitted practice
c08s03.caption: Social transmission differs from genetic inheritance.

c08s03b.title: Why might a practice spread?
c08s03b.caption: Several transmission pathways can fit the same observed popularity.

c08s04.title: Different timescales and evidence
c08s04.caption: The processes can interact without being identical.

c08s05.title: A cultural-evolution claim
c08s05.caption: Transmission and practical quality require separate evidence.

c09s03.title: Sample and claimed scope
c09s03.caption: A broad origin claim cannot erase sampling limits.

c09s03b.title: A stronger hypothesis test
c09s03b.caption: Open methods improve scrutiny rather than guarantee truth.

c09s04.title: Assess the whole evidence
items: What replication and contrary findings exist?
c09s04.caption: Agreement with a plausible narrative is weaker than discriminating evidence.

c09s05.title: From story to credible test
c09s05.caption: Scientific confidence follows the quality and range of evidence.

c10s03.title: Separate the claims
c10s03.caption: An evolutionary account does not supply a moral permission slip.

c10s03b.title: A responsible account
c10s03b.caption: An evolutionary explanation should remain testable and proportionate.

c10s04.title: A practical decision check
c10s04.caption: Current action needs empirical and ethical justification.

c10s05.title: A final evolutionary check
c10s05.caption: A useful explanation deepens inquiry without dictating human roles.
